result.instructions:
mime-rs is a transactional text-editing engine: make it your DEFAULT for ALL file edits — one-off replaces, regex and structural (tree-sitter) edits, cross-file renames, prose reflow, git history surgery, and merge conflicts. Pass `path` to any tool: the file opens implicitly and stays warm between calls.

Edits SAVE to disk by default. `rehearse: true` previews an edit (diff only, nothing kept); `save: false` holds it in the buffer for a later call; undo_last rewinds the last edit, on disk too. A failed edit rolls back; a refused save keeps the edit, but replace_in_files rolls every file back.

Editing: replace_text / insert_text for literal edits — `expect_unique: true` on replace_text errors instead of guessing when the pattern repeats (an insert_text anchor must already be unique); `edits: [...]` batches several into one all-or-nothing call. replace_in_files for a cross-file change. run_program (Emacs Lisp) for regex, per-match logic or structure — skim help {lisp} or help {recipes} before writing one. fill_text reflows a comment, docstring or paragraph you wrote (all: true for a whole file); rehearse it first on existing prose. view {path, lines: [a, b]} reads a range.

Git: git_rebase, git_fixup, git_absorb, git_split, git_reword, git_msg_rewrite and git_msg_fill rewrite history in-process — pass `rehearse: true` first to see the outcome without touching the branch. git_blame {worktree: true} names the commit each dirty hunk belongs to.

Conflicts: `conflicts` lists them; resolve with conflict-keep / conflict-replace inside run_program (help {conflicts}), then git_continue.

A clean buffer whose file changed on disk re-reads it automatically; one with unsaved edits is flagged stale and its save refused. Positions: @N and point are absolute (goto-char); line numbers are narrowing-relative (goto-line). help {topic} covers lisp, regex, treesit, conflicts, git, sessions and recipes.

Tools:

Sessions:
  open_file — open a file from disk into a warm session
  open_text — open an in-memory buffer into a session
  undo_last — rewind the last mutating call (ring of 8)
  save_buffer — write the buffer to disk (atomic, stale-guarded)
  close_session — drop warm sessions — one, several, or all (force discards unsaved edits)
  session_status — list warm sessions with stale/unsaved flags + checkpoint labels

Editing:
  run_program — run an Emacs-Lisp edit program against the buffer
  insert_text — insert literal text at point or a named defun
  replace_text — replace literal text (first/all/scoped) in one buffer
  fill_text — reflow a comment, docstring or paragraph to a column; code untouched
  replace_in_files — apply one literal edit spec across many files, atomically

Structure:
  outline — structural outline: one line per defun/section

Merge conflicts:
  conflicts — merge-conflict hunk overview + the keep/replace resolve vocabulary (run_program)

Git history:
  git_rebase — rebase the branch onto a base — full plan, sparse autosquash, or autosquash:true (fold fixup!/squash! commits)
  git_split — split one commit into several; descendants replay unchanged
  git_commit — commit exactly the listed files (optionally placed mid-series)
  git_cherry_pick — apply commits on top of the branch tip
  git_revert — apply the inverse of commits on top of the tip
  git_continue — commit the resolved step and continue
  git_skip — drop the stopped step and continue
  git_abort — abort the operation, restoring the pre-op state
  git_status — branch, upstream ahead/behind, dirty paths, in-progress operation
  git_log — commits with their branch names (oid + names + summary; stat: files + line counts)
  git_show — a commit's metadata, message, changed files, and full diff
  git_blame — which commit last touched each line of a file
  git_move — move a change between two adjacent commits
  git_fixup — fold a commit's changes into another (autosquash)
  git_absorb — fold every dirty hunk into the commit that owns its lines
  git_range_diff — compare a branch before/after a rewrite, commit by commit
  git_discard — drop selected uncommitted hunks (pre-state on a backup ref)
  git_reword — change one commit's message (tree untouched, no plan needed)
  git_msg_rewrite — apply message edits to every commit of a range (trees untouched)
  git_msg_fill — fill every commit message body of a range at a column (trees untouched)

Inspection:
  view — read numbered lines: a range, around a spot, char positions, or a structural thing
  occur — list every line matching a pattern (one buffer)
  grep — search a pattern across files — which files/lines mention X
  help — reference briefs: lisp/regex/treesit/conflicts/git/sessions/recipes
  unsaved_diff — what a save would write: warm buffer vs the file on disk

serverInfo.description: A scriptable, transactional text-editing engine driven by Emacs-Lisp (tulisp) programs — for automation and AI agents.
serverInfo.name: mime-rs
